findings.description: MA-9's second case is commented as "main() exits while the stderr file is live — both handlers run", but with MI_EXIT=3 the adapter takes `result=$(...) || exit_code=$?`, then `rm -f`, then restores the prior trap via `eval "$prev_exit_trap"`, and only exits later. By the time EXIT fires the chained handler has already been replaced by the original one. The assertion `PRIOR-EXIT-RAN` therefore only proves the restore path (already proven by the success case), not that the chained `rm -f -- "$err_file"; <prior body>` string is well-formed and runs both halves when the process dies with the file live. MA-8 covers TERM-mid-call but without a prior trap, so the one code path this change actually adds (chained body executing) has no test.
findings.failure_mode: A future regression in the chained trap string (e.g. quoting of `prev_exit_body`, a prior body ending in `&` or starting with a comment that swallows the rest) would pass MA-9 and MA-8 unnoticed, and surface only as a lost caller EXIT handler or an orphaned stderr file in production under TERM.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third case modelled on MA-8: set a prior EXIT trap, run the adapter with a `mi` shim that sleeps, send TERM to the adapter mid-call, then assert both that `PRIOR-EXIT-RAN` is on stderr and that `compgen -G "$priv/model-adapter-stderr.*"` finds nothing. Correct the comment on the existing MI_EXIT=3 case to say it exercises the restore path.

findings.description: The diff updates the `rule_key` function comment to include `Bash(:*)` as universal, but the file's header block — the normative grammar statement cited as cycle-126 SDD D-4.5 ("A universal rule (bare Bash, or Bash(*) after trimming) covers every Bash requirement") — still lists only bare `Bash` and `Bash(*)`. The usage text and the header are what operators read when a preflight passes or fails unexpectedly; they now disagree with the implementation on which rules are treated as allow-all / deny-all.
findings.failure_mode: An operator with `Bash(:*)` in a deny list sees every requirement reported denied and, consulting the header, concludes the checker is wrong rather than the settings; conversely a reviewer auditing the grammar against the SDD misses that the empty-prefix form is universal.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the header grammar paragraph (and the SDD D-4.5 text if it is quoted there) to read: "A universal rule (bare Bash, Bash(*), or the empty prefix Bash(:*) after trimming) covers every Bash requirement".
